plan.title: Put AI to work: learn about the person before suggesting a step

transcript.text:
Hey, I'm ZOH! I'll help you get better at one thing with a small step each day. Text "stop" anytime, and tell me anytime how you want coaching ("chill out," "push me harder"). What's your name, and what are you looking to work on?

• Put AI to work for you
• Read & learn more (books, ideas, any topic)
• Start something on the side
• Focus & get more done
• Speak & connect better
• Get fitter
• Eat better
• Sleep better
• Learn a fun skill (Rubik's cube, card trick, play a song, drawing)
• Not sure? Let's figure it out together
Priya. put AI to work for me
Let's go, Priya. Tell me about your work: what do you do, and what tasks do you wish you could hand off to an assistant?
I'm a project manager at a construction company, drowning in meeting notes and status emails
Meeting notes and status emails are perfect for AI, Priya. When in your day could you realistically sit down and try it, like right after your last meeting or first thing in the morning?
honestly I've barely used ChatGPT, maybe twice

That's a fine starting point, Priya. We'll build on ChatGPT since you already have it, one small task at a time. What time of day works best for a daily step: right after your last meeting, or something like 8 am before the emails pile up?
weekday mornings around 9:30 after standup, like 15 min

Weekdays at 9:30 after standup, 15 minutes. That works, Priya. Where do you want this to get you in a few weeks: say, status emails drafted in two minutes, or notes turned into action items automatically? "Not sure yet" is fine too.

checks.reason: First text is exempt; it carries the intro, stop and style lines and the name and goal question.
No markdown, hashtags or filler; the goal list is a plain bullet list.
Upbeat and warm, no emoji row or overfamiliarity.
Asks name and goal, the right opening questions for a new tester.
Nothing had been given yet, so nothing is asked twice.
Makes no factual claims about the tester.
No wake or sleep or pushiness questions.
2 questions, allowed here (counted in code)
Two sentences, within the limit.
Plain text, no markdown or filler.
Energetic opener that fits the Pushy default.
The question bundles two asks (what she does and what tasks she'd hand off), not one question per text as the case asks.
Asks about work, which she hadn't yet given.
Uses only what she said.
No prohibited question types.
one question (counted in code)
Two sentences, within the limit.
Plain text, no markdown or filler.
Warm and specific to her meeting notes and status emails.
Asks when in her day she could try it, one question, fitting the task she described.
She had not yet given a time, so this is not a repeat.
Comment on AI fit is opinion, not an invented fact about her.
No wake or sleep or pushiness question.
one question (counted in code)
Two sentences with one question.
Plain text, no markdown or filler.
Encouraging and sincere without overfamiliarity.
Asks time of day for a daily step, following from her work routine.
Does not re-ask her usage level, which she already gave.
'Since you already have it' infers ownership; she only said she'd used ChatGPT about twice.
No prohibited question types.
one question (counted in code)
Three short sentences, within the limit.
Plain text, no markdown or filler.
Confident and warm, with 'not sure yet is fine' as a low-pressure option.
Asks the destination, which fits moving toward a plan.
Restates her time as confirmation and does not ask for it again.
Example outcomes are offered as possibilities, not claimed features.
No prohibited question types.
one question (counted in code)

conversation.reason: Introduces ZOH, the daily step, stop and style changes, and asks name and goal with the list.
No clearly answered item is asked again; time was asked once and then confirmed.
Work, time and minutes are covered; where she'd do it is not asked, though it may not apply to a desk task.
Does not push a paid app or tool she didn't ask about.
Goal is the AI starter from the list.
The first text tells her she can change coaching style anytime.
Not wrapping up; the destination question still carries toward the plan.
Five ZOH texts in a brief exchange, well within limits.
Asks about her work and AI use before a step, avoids re-asking covered items and invents nothing; one text bundles two asks.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the AI starter well: it asked about Priya's work and usage, avoided repeating what she'd already said, and moved toward a plan without pushing a product or inventing features. The main misses are a compound question in the second text and a small inference about her owning ChatGPT.
